scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot that predates the membership change, isolated together with one committed voter immediately after the restart. Once the isolated node is leader, a client Apply is issued on it and on the majority-side leader if one exists; the partition is then healed and the applied slices of both FSMs are compared. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The isolated node's rebuilt configuration is the three-voter snapshot configuration, so its quorum is two while the committed configuration's quorum is three.
An Apply that returns success is an acknowledged duty for the client.
With the flag off the same isolation cannot produce a leader, so the write has no leader to succeed on.
excluded: Any FSM divergence or lost-entry claim; the probe did not produce a majority-side leader and such a claim needs both sides to write.
The established configuration-loss and minority-election findings, which are recorded separately.

basis.prefix: The harness reuses the same scenario construction as the immediate-isolation experiment (MakeClusterCustom with Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs; a deliberate Snapshot; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged and two AddVoter calls; Shutdown and NewRaft on the same stores with a fresh inmem transport; Partition isolating the restarted node plus one committed voter with the pair reconnected). It then waits for the isolated node to become leader, issues Apply on it and on a majority-side leader when one exists, heals by reconnecting every transport, waits two seconds, and emits mvdiv_after_heal with the leadership outcome, both apply outcomes, the conflict index, the applied entries at that index where available, and the applied slice lengths; no production logic is modified.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the acknowledgement it gives a client: an Apply that reports success must rest on a majority of the committed configuration, which the caller cannot check from the public API.

comparisons.description: A client write must not be acknowledged on the isolated side, whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it is acknowledged.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side has no leader, so the write cannot be acknowledged there.

revision_reason: The divergence harness now emits the startup_before_restart admission event (with mode, snapshots and expected server count) that the declared prerequisites require; the previous execution produced the result events but no admission, so both comparisons could not complete. Scenario, isolation, apply and heal steps and assertions are unchanged.
